sources.entry: Stretto ⚠ - Music player with Youtube/Soundcloud import and iTunes/Spotify discovery. (Demo, Clients) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Stretto is an open source, web-based music player that backs each track with a YouTube or SoundCloud video or song, with a companion Chrome extension for downloading tracks.
summary.what_it_does: Stretto is a web music player where every track in your library is linked to a matching video or song on YouTube or SoundCloud. The README says a companion Chrome extension downloads the tracks to the browser directly. Features listed include importing playlists from Spotify, syncing libraries between machines, automatic lyric fetching for the current song, music discovery through iTunes and Spotify top charts, and searching iTunes to add tracks to a library. It offers multiple themes and works as a progressive web app. The README says it is completely free.
use_cases: Play music from YouTube or SoundCloud in a single library
Import Spotify playlists into a web player
Discover new music through iTunes or Spotify charts
Sync a music library across browsers or machines
Listen to a self-hosted music player on Android via Kiwi browser
how_to_run: Create a .env file with GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID and SOUNDCLOUD_CLIENT_ID
Without Docker: install Node.js 12 and a running MongoDB, and set MONGO_URL in the environment
notable: Backs each track with a YouTube or SoundCloud source instead of hosting audio files
Imports playlists from Spotify and discovers music through iTunes and Spotify charts
Companion Chrome extension handles downloading tracks to the browser
Runs as a progressive web app, with Android use via Kiwi browser
caveats: Relies on a companion Chrome extension to download tracks
Self-hosting needs Google, Spotify and SoundCloud client IDs in a .env file
Non-Docker setup requires Node.js 12 and MongoDB
